source: Land Berlin, Naturdenkmale: Baeume und Findlinge (declared natural monuments)
licence_proof: The dataset's own daten.berlin.de listing (schutzgebiete-und-schutzobjekte-nach-naturschutzrecht-berlin-inklusive-natura-2000-wfs-c36fe3f2) states the licence as 'Datenlizenz Deutschland - Zero - Version 2.0 (dl-de-zero-2.0)', the German public-sector equivalent of CC0: no attribution required, commercial use allowed, no conditions.
designation: Naturdenkmal (Land Berlin), layer schutzgebiete:a_nd, 'Naturdenkmale: Baeume und Findlinge'
attribution: Land Berlin, Senatsverwaltung fuer Mobilitaet, Verkehr, Klimaschutz und Umwelt (not required by the licence, credited anyway)
scope: All 708 features in the WFS layer, filtered to nd_art == 'Baum' (638 of 708; the other 70 are 'Findling', protected boulders, not trees, and excluded here). City-wide, all 12 Bezirke, superseding the per-district daten.berlin.de listings (e.g. the 38-tree Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf page) which are a subset of this same dataset.
caveat: No age field and no girth field, the same gap as Italy's MASAF register: 'schutzgrund' (reason for designation) and 'designated' (ordinance date, mostly 1993-03-02 or a district-specific date, i.e. when it was DECLARED a monument, not when it was planted) are the only date-like fields. Coordinates are the register's own point per tree, already WGS84 via the WFS srsName parameter (no reprojection needed, verified against Vienna's -like precision). 'place' is assembled from free-text hints (hinweise/strasse/hausnummer) and is not a structured address; several entries carry only a Bezirk (district) name. Twin/triplet entries sharing an nd_id root (e.g. 1-10/B-1, 1-10/B-2) are register-level duplicates of the same feature at metres apart, same as Setubal's twins; fold before publishing per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md.
